Gate outcomes follow the decision table, and a warning names the gate that failed
Experience figures follow the disclosure rule for their source
Mandatory and optional sections are correctly classified from their headers
Code excerpts under evaluation are fixed fixtures, so a formatter silently correcting one cannot leave graded cases asserting against an expectation that no longer holds
notes: A stale fixture is our defect, so these are preconditions and carry no priority

requirement_text: A case branch declares which harness ref it runs against, as data carried on the branch rather than a constant in the dependency pin
notes: An extend/ branch needs a harness capability that exists only on stabilization, and no constant pin can express that

requirement_text: A harness commit is used only when its required gate run concluded success on that exact commit, and the absence of a run is never treated as a pass
notes: Every negative is a distinct way for the gate to fail open, and a gate that fails open is indistinguishable from no gate

requirement_text: An unverified harness refuses the run on main and yields an ungated run elsewhere, and an unresolvable ref refuses on any branch
notes: Exit 4, never exit 1: a refusal says no verdict was computable, and exit 1 would read as the model underperforming

requirement_text: The resolver imports nothing from the harness, because it runs before the harness is installed and cannot ask an unverified ref to vouch for itself
notes: A source check, because the defect works on a machine where the harness is already installed and fails only in CI

requirement_text: The code-style rules pylint cannot express are enforced on this tree with the same implementation the harness uses
notes: One project across two repositories: a rule enforced on one side only holds until somebody moves a file

requirement_text: The shipped task and rule corpus loads through the real loaders and satisfies referential integrity R1 through R5
notes: The harness proves the loaders work; nothing said whether THIS corpus loads. Authoring hit two shape errors no schema test could catch

requirement_text: Every constraint kind the corpus states is registered, so the open vocabulary does not fragment through unread warnings
notes: The harness warns rather than failing by design, so a warning nobody reads is how a vocabulary fragments

requirement_text: The ablation control states no constraint and its rule checks none, so the 30001 and 30002 pair measures instruction following rather than habit
notes: Verified against an injected constraint WITH a matching check: R2 and R3 both pass and this case still fails, which is the gap it exists for

requirement_text: The instruction-following corpus supplies the six tasks and six rule sets that cases 30001 to 30009 dispatch and judge against
notes: The ablation pair is the measurement; 10425 protects it because no integrity check can

requirement_text: The grounding corpus supplies the six tasks and six rule sets that cases 30010 to 30015 dispatch and judge against, with exact figures and a designed fabrication target
notes: Figures are exact so alteration is an assertion rather than a judgement; GND_005 is an asymmetric pair because one task cannot ask for both

requirement_text: Every taxonomy code the corpus attaches to a finding is registered in the harness, so a finding cannot carry an invented code
notes: Six invented codes were authored where the registry already carried the right ones; 10143 to 10145 read design documents and emitted codes, never a data file

requirement_text: The ambiguity corpus supplies the three tasks that cases 30016 to 30018 dispatch, as an ablation pair varying whether the input is answerable
notes: Neither task alone measures the requirement: a model that always asks passes AMB_001 and fails AMB_002, and one that never asks does the reverse. The requirement is discrimination

requirement_text: Every task tagged control states no constraint and its rule set checks none, so an ablation control cannot be destroyed by an edit
notes: Generalised from one named task to a property over the corpus when a second ablation pair arrived; a control added later is protected without editing the case

requirement_text: The requirement matching corpus supplies one posting and three resumes landing exactly on the three rows of the gate decision table
notes: 7.8 of 10 is a fractional credit on a five-item AND list, not a rounding; it is the only way a ten-requirement posting reaches 78.0

requirement_text: The connector cases hold the candidate fixed and vary only the connector, so reading a disjunction as a conjunction is observable
notes: The same candidate scores 100 percent or 33 percent on the same line depending only on how the connector was read

requirement_text: The experience cases distinguish a stated figure from a derived one, so a numeric fabrication check is directional rather than exact
notes: Stating 8+ while holding fifteen is true; the obvious implementation flags the correct behaviour as a violation, which is why 30026 exists

requirement_text: Every evaluation family this repository's matrix names is registered in the harness, so a value reaching the durable record is resolvable
notes: T5 compares two fields of one row and neither is the registry; the harness cannot run this check without reading a file this repo owns

requirement_text: Every code excerpt inlined into a task is byte-identical to the guarded fixture it names, so the dispatched copy is the copy under guard
notes: ContextDocument carries inline content and has no file reference, so a task supplying an excerpt holds a second copy that 10401 to 10403 do not examine

requirement_text: The code comprehension corpus supplies nine tasks formulating three grounding requirements in the code domain
notes: The family brings no requirements of its own: a grounding requirement is domain-independent and the formulation exists to show the behaviour survives a change of domain

requirement_text: The settlement excerpt guard executes all three money outcomes, including the silent zero settlement
notes: The guard asserted the negative settlement and both raising cases and never the zero, so the outcome the family exists to catch was not itself under guard

requirement_text: A debug workflow runs one test or a subset in its own jobs, yields no verdict, and takes both refs as inputs so a case can be run against a harness other than the one its branch maps to
notes: The harness had two diagnostic workflows and this repository had none, so the side where graded cases live could not run one case and look at it

requirement_text: A debug run judges a failed case and the gate does not, because the rubric is what separates a wrong case from a wrong model
notes: A failed assertion says the case did not pass and not whether the case or the model is wrong; those prompt entirely different fixes

requirement_text: Every authored rubric anchor carries an exemplar, so calibration can measure judge drift against a known intended level
notes: 108 anchors carried descriptions and no exemplars, so the drift detector the harness design specifies had nothing to detect with

requirement_text: A level 5 exemplar passes the assertions of the rule it belongs to, since a case cannot award a top score through a failed gate
notes: An incoherent top exemplar would make calibration report drift every time the judge behaved correctly

requirement_text: The code comprehension task file is reproducible from its shipped generator, so a hand edit to a generated file is reported
notes: The generator lived outside the repository, so a fixture change left 10428 failing with no shipped way to regenerate

requirement_text: Every pair a graded case names is one the corpus builds, so a task and rule that exist separately and were never joined is reported without dispatching anything
notes: A case named a task and a rule that both existed and were never joined, so case_for raised KeyError; it was masked by a failing foundation for every run before it surfaced

requirement_text: A recorded response that withheld content states the provider's own reason for withholding it, so a refusal is not read as a model failure
notes: Two adapters shipped a refusal that did not say so. A gemini double of the wrong shape reported 50015 as a model failure for three recorded runs, and the Claude adapter mapped stop_reason refusal to the canonical value while leaving block_reason empty, reporting 50013 the same way. Both were corrected inside one adapter, which is what let the second happen

requirement_text: Every graded case's declared foundations are exactly the ones its design inventory states, so a dependency cannot be added in code without a document approving it
notes: Six dependencies shipped that section 9.10.2 forbids, two cases carrying two each, and the table they contradict covered nine cases of twenty-one. For claude-opus-5-5 they suppressed eight measurements and one confirmed finding, 50004, behind a root-vector failure

requirement_text: Every security case declares every vector its payload carries and names the one it is about, so an incidental match cannot stand in for coverage
notes: Asserting that a payload matches some registered vector is satisfied by an incidental match, which is how task_substitution and tool_coercion looked screened while having no vector at all

requirement_text: Every tracked document and data file in this repository carries an MIT SPDX header, including the corpus the licence rationale names as material people copy and adapt
notes: The corpus is the material most likely to travel and carried no licence marker at all

requirement_text: The graded gate job replays both sides, so it needs no provider credential and the gate stays credential-free
notes: Before judge fixtures a graded gate meant a live judge call per passing case, which A1 keeps out of this workflow

requirement_text: The live workflow runs the three jobs in sequence, each needing the one before it, so a red rung stops the ladder
notes: Running the judge live after our code changed a frozen outcome spends quota to rediscover something established

requirement_text: Every workflow that installs the harness takes a commit resolved in the same run, and the workflow that spends quota most of all
notes: Quota spent measuring a model with an unverified instrument attributes our defect to the model under test

requirement_text: A workflow that spends provider quota does not start when the paired harness commit is not green
notes: An ungated free run still yields a marked artifact; an ungated live run has nothing to offer in exchange for the quota

requirement_text: A refusal stops every test-executing job in a gating workflow, so a red harness on a regression run spends nothing
notes: A job carrying a status function, or one that never named the resolver in its needs, runs against a red harness anyway

requirement_text: The debug workflow is not blocked by a red harness, because debugging happens against a harness branch in development
notes: Refusing to debug against a harness that is not green withholds the tool exactly when it is needed

requirement_text: The operator runbook names only workflows that exist and inputs they declare, so a documented dispatch is one that works
notes: A dispatch naming an undeclared input is rejected by GitHub, and the reader concludes the procedure is broken rather than the page

requirement_text: A branch referent naming a case identifier resolves against this repository's inventory, so a typo is caught on first push
notes: An identifier that binds to nothing has cost this project real time before

requirement_text: The pairing mapping covers every branch kind CI runs on, so a dated branch cannot silently take the default pairing
notes: A stabilization branch falling through to the default would run against main while looking configured

requirement_text: A pull request resolves its harness from the head branch and its strictness from the target, taking the stricter of the two
notes: A stabilization branch merging into main resolved the advisory entry, so code could land on main never measured with a green harness

requirement_text: Every file read and write in this repository declares an encoding, enforced by the same checker the harness uses
notes: One rule, one implementation, two roots

requirement_text: The obfuscation payloads survive a real load carrying the code points they are made of, and still match their vectors
notes: The canary assertions are ASCII and would keep passing against a mangled payload, so nothing else would notice

requirement_text: A rule serving a graded evaluation case carries a rubric, so omitting one cannot quietly turn it into a deterministic case
notes: A rule with no rubric now passes on its deterministic checks, so omitting one is consequential and must be visible

requirement_text: Every requirement traced in this repository's matrix is also stated in its test plan, and every stated one is traced
notes: Thirty-nine requirements were traced and stated nowhere, because the check that would have found it lived only in the harness

requirement_text: The model states the cause of a defect and not only the outcomes that follow from it
notes: 30036 asserts three outcomes that all follow from one cause, so listing them scored the same as diagnosing it

requirement_text: The model states the determinate remedy for a defect it identifies, where the correct behaviour follows from the stated semantics
notes: Identification and remediation are different claims; a review that finds a money-moving defect and proposes nothing is incomplete

requirement_text: The model recommends bounding an unbounded design, and names the data the bound would require
notes: P4: the module is not wrong to omit an expiry, it is weaker for it, so its absence cannot turn a run red

requirement_text: Every test named by a traceability matrix row is defined by this suite, so a requirement cannot read as covered by a case that was never written
notes: 10447 was inventoried, traced and cited by two docstrings while absent; 10401-10405 were renamed and the matrix kept the old slugs

requirement_text: The case, requirement, graded-case, corpus and task figures stated in README.md are recomputed from the repository, so the front page cannot describe work that is absent or omit work that exists
notes: Every figure had drifted and the graded-case row read 'designed, not yet written' while all 69 were written

requirement_text: A harness gate that has not concluded is waited for within a bounded budget rather than refused, while a red conclusion, an absent run and an exhausted wait are each refused at once
notes: Four consecutive paired pushes produced a red consumer run cleared by a manual re-run of the identical job

requirement_text: Harness files are located through the installed package and never by directory traversal to an adjacent checkout, the engine roster resolves and names engines, and a run's flags and its candidate engine reach the plan the judge channel is actually built from
notes: Gate 4 failed in CI reading ../AP-Harness-QC/config/engines.yaml, which exists only where both repositories are checked out side by side

requirement_text: A deterministic assertion tests the claim a case is about and not the wording an answer happened to use, so a correct response phrased differently is not reported as a finding about the model
notes: First graded run: eight failures, seven of them this corpus or the harness screen reporting a correct answer; three surfaced as QC_LLM_INCONSISTENT because the assertions read wording that varied between observations

requirement_text: The graded layers run as one job per priority band per platform, named so that a red states which remedy applies, with the preconditions in a job of their own and the band outcomes carried between them
notes: One job ran Gate 2 and Gate 4, so a red meant either our defect or the model's; reading it meant finding the case and looking up its priority. The first band condition used !cancelled(), which 10439 reported as outrunning the resolver's refusal

requirement_text: A band below P1 is judged against the pass floor rather than by any failure, counts skipped cases outside the denominator, and refuses rather than scoring a band whose report carries an error
notes: P0 and P1 need no rate because a failure there is V1 by itself. An error is our defect and the floor is about the model, so averaging one in would let a broken run read as a model that nearly cleared the bar

requirement_text: Every graded case binds a task and rule pair no other graded case binds, so a red names the claim that failed rather than the conjunction of four
notes: Four cases dispatched one task with one rule and asserted the conjunction of its four assertions, so one failing assertion failed all four and three reported a finding about something they never measured

requirement_text: Every inventory row in this repository's design and test plan names a case the suite implements, reported so an unbuilt design is visible rather than forgotten
notes: The harness check read this checkout for one day and could pass only on a machine holding both repositories, failing CI on both platforms. Each side checks its own inventories, which is the boundary CLAUDE.md states

requirement_text: Every workflow invocation emits both JUnit XML and Allure raw results, so a debug or graded run produces the reporting evidence the downstream artifact contract requires and not half of it
notes: debug-cases-on-demand.yml emitted JUnit with no Allure, so the workflow reached for when something has already gone wrong produced no report. Found in the harness, where four invocations across both repositories were in that state and nothing read a workflow against the mandate

requirement_text: The judge engine a run names on the command line is the engine that grades it, so the judge recorded in result metadata is the instrument that produced the scores
notes: judge_binding passed a literal empty string where the judge engine goes, so --judge-engine openai graded with gemini while the recorded metadata named openai. The harness implements the documented precedence correctly and was reached with an empty first term

requirement_text: The observation count a run names on the command line is the count dispatched, so a run that measured a different population is distinguishable from one that did not
notes: The flag was read into observation_count as an override above the roster entry, and nothing varied it and asserted the dispatched population changed. The case also pins that an override still earns escalation
